pass_summary: LGG's best-supported GI outcome is antibiotic-associated diarrhea prevention in children (tier A); acute gastroenteritis treatment, infant colic, and IBS abdominal pain show moderate benefit (tier B/C), several capped by heterogeneity or a fragile subgroup effect rather than by absence of evidence. A notable caution: RCT-pooled evidence favors LGG for necrotizing enterocolitis prevention in preterm infants, but a real-world NICU cohort found the opposite direction and rare sepsis cases exist in that population - recorded here and flagged for the safety pass. Traveler's diarrhea prevention was tested and came back essentially null.

claims.population_detail: children treated with antibiotics for any reason
claims.tier_rationale: Szajewska & Kolodziej 2015 SR (Aliment Pharmacol Ther), 11 RCTs pooled overall (n=1308, RR 0.49 [0.29-0.83], low-quality GRADE); significance is driven entirely by the children subgroup (5 RCTs, n=445, RR 0.48 [0.26-0.89], moderate-quality GRADE) - adults alone were not significant (6 RCTs, n=863, RR 0.48 [0.20-1.15], low-quality), except a Helicobacter pylori-eradication antibiotic subset (4 RCTs, n=280, RR 0.26 [0.11-0.59]). Row scoped to children per tier rule 5; the adult null and H. pylori-subset finding are noted here rather than built as separate rows, since no dedicated adult-only SR exists to grade them from.

claims.effect_size: MD -0.85 day [-1.15, -0.56] duration of diarrhea (SR, 15 of 18 trials pooled for this outcome)
claims.tier_rationale: Szajewska et al. 2019 update SR, 18 RCTs (n=4208); stool volume showed no effect, duration of diarrhea was reduced (15 RCTs, n=3820). The review's own abstract flags 'high heterogeneity and methodological limitations of the included trials', which caps this at tier C by definition regardless of the large pooled N. A recent large RCT (NEJM, ~943 children) included in this pooling found no benefit, driving consistency to mixed; effect was stronger in European cohorts and at doses >=10^10 CFU/day.
claims.dose: 10^9-10^12 CFU/day across pooled trials; >=10^10 CFU/day showed greater effect

claims.population_detail: mostly children with IBS (4 of 5 RCTs pediatric; diagnostic criteria varied by trial)
claims.effect_size: significant reduction in abdominal pain severity, I2=25.9% (SR of 5 LGG-only RCTs; pooled RR/MD not reported in abstract)
claims.tier_rationale: Maslennikov et al. 2026 strain-specific SR (single-strain LGG-vs-placebo RCTs only), RoB2-assessed. Pain was the only outcome poolable for LGG - 'other IBS symptoms and quality of life indicators could not be meta-analyzed'. The pooled benefit is fragile: it was lost across all subgroups when trials were stratified by IBS diagnostic criteria, and the dose-response was non-monotonic (benefit only at ~6x10^9 CFU/day, not at 2x10^10 or 4x10^10). Modest pooled N and that inconsistency cap this at B rather than A.
claims.dose: 6x10^9 CFU/day (effect not replicated at 2x10^10 or 4x10^10 CFU/day in the same pool)
claims.duration: 8 weeks (effect not seen at 4 or 6 weeks)
claims.notes: roster_source's shorthand cites this SR under gi-ibs-global; the outcome it actually grades is abdominal pain, so the claim is filed under gi-ibs-pain. Other IBS symptoms and QoL were not poolable for this strain.

claims.tier_rationale: Liu et al. 2024 SR, Cochrane RoB2 tool. Modest pooled N (168) across only 4 trials, and at least one included trial (~4.5x10^9 CFU/day, 4 weeks) reported crying time comparable to placebo while others found large reductions - that inconsistency and the small pool cap this at B. Secondary marker: fecal calprotectin also fell (MD -103.28 ug/g [-149.30, -7.26]).

claims.effect_size: RR 0.50 [0.26, 0.93], p=0.03, NEC >=Stage II (SR of 5 LGG-only RCTs)
claims.tier_rationale: Ananthan et al. 2024 strain-specific SR (Cochrane methodology), RCT-only pooled estimate for LGG as sole probiotic. The RR is real but close to the null (CI upper bound 0.93) on only 5 trials. Consistency is marked mixed because a separate single-center before/after cohort (outside this SR) found NEC incidence rose after routine LGG adoption (10.2% to 16.8%), and rare LGG sepsis has been reported in preterm infants specifically - a genuine real-world caution alongside the RCT-level benefit. That tension, not the RCT evidence alone, is why this caps at B rather than A.
claims.safety_flags: A conflicting single-center observational cohort found higher NEC incidence after routine LGG use in a NICU; rare LGG sepsis has been reported in preterm infants. See safety-bacteremia in safety.json.

claims.effect_size: trend toward reduced incidence, not significant (p=0.08); pooled RR not reported for the LGG subgroup
claims.tier_rationale: McFarland 2007 SR pooled 12 trials of various probiotics for traveler's diarrhea (overall sRR 0.85 [0.79-0.91]); LGG's own subgroup (6 RCTs, 9 treatment arms) reached only a non-significant trend (p=0.08). A null result is as much a finding as a positive one and this is a formal strain-specific subgroup of an SR, so it is graded rather than excluded - but the subgroup's own RR/CI was not reported, only a p-value, which is why this stays at B instead of A.

gaps: No strain-attributable evidence found for gi-cdiff-prevention specifically: existing trials combine LGG with other strains (e.g. L. reuteri, PLACIDE's mixed lactobacilli/bifidobacteria), and tier rule 6 blocks decomposing those pools. gi-hpylori-adjunct: no dedicated eradication-adjunct trial data beyond the AAD subgroup noted above.
